title: Hey all new to the sub, but I’ve got a complete same design document and zero coding knowledge, but I have the whole thing written and plotted out, can these new tools make my vision a reality?
author: Braunb8888

comments.author: Minimum_Lock_1906
comments.body: A AI vai conseguir te ajudar muito na implementação, porém minimamente você precisará aprender sobre arquitetura de softwares para entender o que ela está construindo e guia-la pelo melhor caminho

comments.author: StellarSoupStudio
comments.body:
Try it out, there will likely be a bunch of additional questions you'll have to answer but the coding agent should prompt you.

  
AI coding does still require some knowledge of how code works but, the advantage is you have the LLM to ask questions about and it's nicer than stackoverflow.

  
If you have specific questions though and want a human response feel free to ask lol.

replies.author: StellarSoupStudio
replies.body: First things first what type of game is it? 2D Platformer, 3D game, Visual Novel, ect?

replies.author: Braunb8888
replies.body: I have an RPG in mind. Third person. Have the whole world and characters and dialogue already written. Combat system mapped out. Just no coding ability or budget haha.

replies.author: StellarSoupStudio
replies.body:
So for AI dev with no coding experience I first recommend learning git. You just need to know enough to get the game set up. For engine Godot will probably be best.

You can probably craft a prompt like this:

"Hi (insert LLM name here) I'm a new game developer with no experience in coding, can you give me a step by step guide on how to set up my environment for game development. We will be making a 3rd person RPG. I've been told that we should set up Git and use Godot for development. For context my computer is: (Mac/Windows/Linux)."

Then follow the steps and if you get any error codes, copy the text or screen shot it and put it back in the same chat.

replies.author: Braunb8888
replies.body: What’s the name of the program I need to buy or download?

replies.author: StellarSoupStudio
replies.body: Git and Godot are free. I'd recommend setting up a Github account. Also feel free to DM me if you need more help lol

comments.author: olafthemanofsnow
comments.body: Whilst AI will help massively, understanding what it is doing and how game development works will save you tons of time. Like anything though, it is just about practice.

comments.author: _HoundOfJustice
comments.body:
Probably yes, but dont get overconfident and expect to be able to make a AAA game and especially not expect to ship a serious game within few weeks. Its going to take a while and also it will be expensive. Also the question is what about the creative side of gamedev? Are you going to use premade assets, make them yourself or use AI to generate? 
Im a pro artist so i have no difficulties to bring my own vision to life - but it takes time and even genAI cant change that unless i heavily compromise.

comments.author: sevenoutdb
comments.body: If you want to DM me I can help you get a jumpstart on development. I have been a game producer for >25 years and have been doing mentoring for decades. I can help you get started, talk about your goals, I can even review your game design doc… no, I’m not interested in stealing anyone’s ideas, I’ve got plenty of my own. I don’t want anything from you, so just to be clear, I can help you get started for free.

comments.author: StarMonkeyGames
comments.body:
Yes and No.

Yes: AI bridges the skill required to make software (and whatever else that comes up).

No: It still takes a lot of time. Iteration. Rejection. You still need to figure out programming. Figure out Art. Figure out Marketing.

Like AI can help you learn these things. I have never seen anything like it. An interactive digital library that can teach you whatever you want to learn. And with enough effort, you can do it.

But it's not like AI will do it for you. AI doesn't have good taste and it doesn't understand what you are going for.

It feels like being a high level manager with an idiot savant intern that doesn't really understand you because its not human.

comments.author: rrcecil
comments.body: If your game can run headless in a terminal view basically then that should be the first goal. Then doing gameplay bits to completions (combat module, fishing module, city explorer module, mini game etc) make sure to spend time planning that and having version control THEN you layer on art assets after that (might be something you can do, something AI can help with but not so easily). Make it work in an engine as well, don’t reinvent the wheel.

replies.author: Braunb8888
replies.body: What tools should I look to get started with?

replies.author: rrcecil
replies.body:
honestly I'd start with:  
\-Claude Code (the desktop app)  
\-Godot (free engine)  
\-GitHub so you can always roll back.

Like you describe what you want, it builds it, you play it and give notes. Get one fight or system working with no art first, have it write a plan before each piece, THEN layer on art. Start small, not the whole doc. Make sure to setup rules and guardrails but u can always adjust later.

I’m semi technical, but honestly pretend you’re the director and you’re managing a team. You’ll have to do stuff but make Claude do it, and if it can’t it’s usually not that hard. Feel free to DM me if you get stuck.

Keep to working on one game, and optimize to token usage.

Edit: I could get WAY more complicated here, but run some research on how to setup an efficient project from this sub and YouTube and aggregate everything you like.  
I break things up into roles. I have a Project Manager Agent that updates a dashboard and monitors closing out high token agents and overall.

I have a Build lead that codes one small piece at a time and has to pass the tests before anything merges, an Art lead that makes and checks the art, a Test lead that runs thousands of automated fights and plays each build to file bugs, and a Sound lead. Each one runs helpers for the actual work, I just answer their questions (multiple choice so it's fast) and approve stuff. Then I’ll test it at intervals. It’ll try and build in three.js that won’t scale if you want to get it on console.

comments.author: Virtual-Bottle-8604
comments.body: Yes but it'll be a crude but visually polished prototype thats hard to iterate on. Stephan 3D AI on YouTube as demonstrated the way to get claude to do just that.
